newsitem.title: USA: U.S. firms to cooperate on missile defense.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firms to cooperate on missile defense.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp., Raytheon Co. and TRW Inc. announced on Tuesday the formation of a joint company that could help build a comprehensive defence against ballistic missile attack.
The three defence firms said they would each equally own the venture, to be called United Missile Defence Co., with headquarters in suburban Crystal City, Va.

In a joint release, they noted that each possessed unique experience in areas ranging from land- and sea-based missiles to strategic and tactical radar warning systems and battle management command and control.

The Clinton administration has scaled back the "Star Wars" dream of former President Ronald Reagan of developing a costly umbrella defence of the United States against a massive nuclear missile attack.

But Republicans in Congress are pressing the Pentagon to expand its now-limited Ballistic Missile Defence Organisation (BMDO) plan to protect only U.S. forces and bases from missile attack until a broader threat emerges after the Cold War.
Executives of the three big companies suggested the joint venture was being formed to both meet the needs of the current limited programme and to be prepared for any future expansion.

No financial figures were announced regarding costs of the joint venture. Raytheon, Lockheed Martin and TRW will continue their separate missile businesses, said Bob Hayden, business manager for the venture.

"Developing a system to protect the American people and the freedoms we hold dear is a special responsibility. UMDC is committed to performing this vital role for our nation," said Lockheed Martin Chairman Norman Augustine.

"The uncertain world we live in makes it critical that our nation be protected against the full range of threats we face. Foremost among these is the threat of a limited ballistic missile attack by unfriendly governments," said TRW Chairman Joseph Gorman.
Lockheed Martin's missile and space division in Sunnyvale, Calif., is a leading supplier of missiles and spacecraft to military, government and commercial communications organisations.
Raytheon, with headquarters in Lexington, Mass., is a leading international high-technology company with extensive operations in commercial and defence electronics, engineering and construction.

TRW Systems Integration Group, headquartered in Fairfax, Va., is a leader in the development and application of systems engineering, systems integration, information systems and software development products and services for defence and civil space markets.
